text:
sophia: Heads-up: rolling out a new "Usage Velocity Policy" next week to smooth bursty traffic and reduce noisy overage incidents. This introduces a 1-minute rolling velocity metric that can trigger short 'debit holdbacks' when sustained throughput exceeds your reserved capacity. Full policy + FAQ: https://redwood.internal/policies/usage-velocity (proto)
maria: Can you clarify: is this different from existing rate limits? i.e., will customers see 429s or soft throttles?
sophia: Good question. It's layered: we still have per-second rate limits. Velocity is a longer-window protection to avoid large token spikes shredding latency for others. Typical outcome is a brief holdback (<= 30s) or temporary degraded throughput, not immediate 429s. We only escalate to hard throttles when other signals match.
darren: How does this affect Dedicated customers with reserved capacity vs hosted pay-as-you-go?
sophia: Dedicated: policy respects reserved capacity and only applies if usage pattern is extremely bursty vs the pool config. Hosted (pay-as-you-go): more likely to see holdbacks during extreme velocity. We're adding a dashboard flag so teams can opt into more aggressive smoothing.
els: Are there billing implications? If a holdback delays requests, do customers lose credits or still get billed for tokens generated?
sophia: Billing is unchanged: tokens generated are billed. The holdback prevents additional tokens from being produced during the hold period. Finance will publish a note about adjustments for auto-refunds in edge cases.
finance-bot: FYI: automated rebate flow will run for confirmed system-side throttles that were the sole cause of failed completions. Details in the finance FAQ.
allison: We need a customer communication plan. Timing? What do we tell users who panic about 'debit holdbacks' wording?
sophia: Draft message: "We're introducing a traffic-smoothing measure to protect latency and stability; in rare cases requests may be briefly delayed to avoid large cost spikes and service degradation." We'll avoid the word 'debit' in public messaging — use 'traffic smoothing' or 'temporary request pacing'.
support: Putting playbook into the support runbook now (steps: check velocity chart, run mitigation command, escalate to infra if persistent). ETA for playbook: EOD today.
maria: Any quick mitigation knobs for apps? e.g., client retries or backoff guidance?
sophia: Recommend exponential backoff 500ms -> 2s with jitter, and prefer idempotent requests where possible. We'll surface a header in responses: X-Redwood-Velocity-Hold: true so SDKs can detect and respect pacing.
darren: Can we include a curl sample in the docs showing the header detection?
sophia: Yes. Example snippet to include:
```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
# look for: X-Redwood-Velocity-Hold: true
```
eli: Deploy schedule?
sophia: Staged rollout starting Mon 09:00 PT to 10% hosts, ramp to 100% over 48h if no anomalies. Canary alert if SLO latency increase > 5% or error rate jumps.
allison: Customer comms plan: pre-announce to top 100 customers Tues morning, general blog post Wed, in-console banner Wed afternoon. Support snippet ready.
support: Confirmed — playbook pushed. We'll add KB article with sample wording and troubleshooting steps.
finance-bot: Note for billing: no changes to invoice line-items for this rollout. Any exceptions handled case-by-case.
ops-bot: Canary deployment started (canary id: vel-2026-01). Monitoring dashboards: velocity-chart, holdbacks-per-minute, p99 latency.
maria: Thanks — please ping #customer-ops before public blog so we can prepare CSRs.
sophia: Will do. TL;DR: usage-velocity smoothing to reduce noisy overages, short debit holdbacks possible, SDK header + backoff guidance, staged rollout Mon. Feedback welcome. :rocket:
